title: SDK: add experimentStickyKey option + expose assigned variant on responses
author: Dylan Brooks
description: Context: Route-level experiments require deterministic assignment. The platform supports a stickiness key (preferred: stable per end-user or per tenant) that the router uses when bucketing a request into a variant. This PR adds an optional experimentStickyKey field to the TS SDK request options and includes small helpers to read the assigned {experiment_id, variant_id} from response headers so customers can log/debug assignments. Summary of changes: 1) New request option: experimentStickyKey?: string on chat/completions/embeddings/rerank request option types. When present, the SDK sends header X-Redwood-Experiment-Sticky-Key (exact casing handled by fetch). 2) New response metadata: the SDK now captures experiment assignment headers (x-redwood-experiment-id, x-redwood-experiment-variant, x-redwood-experiment-config-version) and exposes them via response.experimental?.assignment for non-streaming calls. 3) Streaming support: for stream responses, assignment headers are available immediately from the initial response; we surface them on the returned stream handle as stream.experimental.assignment and also provide an onResponse callback hook for callers that want to log headers before consuming tokens. 4) Ergonomics: add helper parseExperimentAssignment(headers) and type ExperimentAssignment to avoid callers hand-parsing header names. 5) Docs + examples: update README snippets for route experiments usage and add a troubleshooting note (stickiness key should be high-entropy; do not default to IP; prefer customer_user_id or customer_session_id). Backwards compatibility: option is fully optional and does not change behavior when omitted. No breaking changes to existing response shapes (new fields are additive under .experimental). Testing: unit tests for header injection + parsing, and one integration-style test with mocked fetch verifying streaming handle includes assignment. Notes: header names align with platform OTel conventions and ADR-047/048; the SDK intentionally does not attempt to generate a default stickiness key to avoid low-entropy skew (see recent beta issue).
commits: feat(client): accept experimentStickyKey and send X-Redwood-Experiment-Sticky-Key header
feat(types): add ExperimentAssignment + experimental response metadata
feat(streaming): expose assignment on stream handle and add onResponse hook
test: add coverage for header parsing and request header injection
docs: update README + add route experiments snippet
changed_files: src/client/request.ts (inject experiment sticky key header; plumb onResponse)
src/types/requestOptions.ts (add experimentStickyKey to request option types)
src/streaming/stream.ts (attach experimental metadata to stream handle)
implementation_notes: Header contract: X-Redwood-Experiment-Sticky-Key is the only new request header added here. Response contract: SDK reads x-redwood-experiment-id, x-redwood-experiment-variant, and x-redwood-experiment-config-version. If headers are missing, assignment is undefined and the helper returns null. Streaming: because fetch exposes headers on the Response before reading the body, assignment is always available even if attribution later drops in telemetry; this is intended for client-side logging only and should not be used as a source of truth for analytics.
review_conversation: Jordan Lee: Can we confirm the stickiness header name matches what the policy engine expects? We recently standardized on X-Redwood-Experiment-Sticky-Key (not the older X-Redwood-Sticky-Key).
Dylan Brooks (author): Yep, using X-Redwood-Experiment-Sticky-Key. Added a small constant + tests to prevent regressions. Also updated README to match.
Logan Wright: Please make sure we don’t accidentally increase header cardinality in logs by default. Are we logging the stickiness key anywhere?
Dylan Brooks (author): SDK does not log headers. Also added note in docs: do not log raw stickiness keys; if needed, hash client-side.
Jada Williams: For streaming, how does a caller access the assigned variant? They won’t have the full response object.
Dylan Brooks (author): Added stream.experimental.assignment and an onResponse callback so they can log assignment before token iteration. Included a snippet in README.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Any RBAC/security concerns with surfacing experiment_id/variant_id to customers? Should we gate it?
Dylan Brooks (author): Platform already sends these headers in beta/GA; this PR only makes them accessible. If an account isn’t enabled, headers won’t be present. No new sensitive data introduced.
Jordan Lee: Minor: parse helper should handle Header objects and plain records. Some frameworks provide a map-like interface.
Dylan Brooks (author): Updated parseExperimentAssignment to accept Headers | Record<string,string> | Array<[string,string]>. Added tests.
Jada Williams: Looks good after the streaming doc update. Approving.
Logan Wright: Approved. Thanks for keeping it additive under .experimental.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK: add optional experimentStickyKey request option and expose experiment assignment (experiment_id/variant_id) via response.experimental.assignment and stream.experimental.assignment for route experiments debugging.
